correctness.rationale: Using π_n=(1−ρ)ρ^{n−1} and decreasing f=c+∑d_k 1_{n≤k}, the geometric memoryless moment formulas for E[N min(N,k)] and E[min(N,k)min(N,l)] yield exactly the displayed positive quadratic deficit; all kernels strictly positive on drops for 0<ρ<1. For p≥2, ℓp(π) dominates ℓ2(π). Constant sequences achieve √(1+ρ)/(1−ρ), nonconstant cone sequences are strict. Weighted unilateral-shift resolvent gives separate unrestricted norm (1−√ρ)^{−1}. Independent rational arithmetic checked 180 eventually constant monotone cases with exact tails.
residual_risks: Finite rational cases are corroboration only; infinite-sequence identity rests on geometric expectation algebra.
The inequality is for nonnegative decreasing inputs only; no extrapolation to 1≤p<2 or arbitrary weights.

evidence: 2015 Kalybay et al. Theorems 2.1/5.2 classify boundedness and compare best constants under more general weights/kernels; their broader domain alone does not algebraically fix the sharp model-specific constant and exact quadratic kernel.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Specialization of an abstract weighted criterion is not assumed to imply an exact sharp norm or positive remainder without derivation. Lack of access is recorded; any subsequently found theorem explicitly implying the formula would reverse this judgment.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge mathematical distinction: sharp constant on the nonnegative decreasing cone with COMMON geometric input/output weights, cross exponent p>=2 to q=2, and an exact strictly positive quadratic drop-kernel remainder. General weighted cone-Hardy criteria and same-exponent weighted mean inequalities located do not state that precise remainder. Older Bennett–Grosse-Erdmann complete text remains inaccessible and is a named priority risk, not affirmative coverage.

checked_sources: General monotone Hardy criteria (Kalybay et al. 2015) and primary proof kernel
value.rationale: A sharp weighted operator norm and exact coercive monotone-cone quadratic deficit are intrinsically useful nontrivial stability information. Geometric probability weights form a natural model and the strict difference from unrestricted Hilbert norm isolates the actual effect of order restrictions; constants and unique extremizers are precise, not generic textbook comparability.
residual_risks: No claim of general all-weight Hardy inequality.
